First, I would NOT quit my job. I'd use my 9-to-5 to fund the season where I learn how to build something of my own. And I wouldn't start by asking: “What digital product should I make?” I'd start by asking: “What problem can I help someone solve?” Because that's where a sellable digital product begins. Here's the process I'd follow: 1. Pick a specific person. Don't create for “everyone who wants to make money” or “women who want a better life.” Get specific. Who are they? What are they trying to accomplish? What's frustrating them right now? 2. Find a problem they already want solved. Look through comments, Reddit threads, Facebook groups, search suggestions, reviews and your own DMs. Pay attention to questions people ask repeatedly. Your goal isn't to invent demand. It's to recognize it. 3. Create the smallest useful solution. Your first product doesn't need 97 modules. Could the solution be a: → guide → template → workbook → checklist → prompt collection → mini-course → toolkit Solve one specific problem well. 4. Validate before you spend weeks creating. Talk about the problem in your content. Teach around it. Ask questions. Watch what gets saves, shares, comments and DMs. You're looking for evidence that people care about the problem before building an entire product around it. 5. Build content around the problem, not the product. This is a big one. If you sell a budgeting template, don't make every post: “Buy my budgeting template.” Create content about overspending, saving, organizing finances, common budgeting mistakes and the outcome your audience wants. Your product becomes the next step, not the entire conversation. 6. Learn how to sell. Creating the PDF is not the business. Learning how to position it, communicate its value, create demand and consistently get it in front of the right people is what turns a digital file into an actual offer. And then? Repeat. Improve. Listen to your customers. Make the product better.  Build your audience. Don't put the pressure of “this needs to replace my salary next month” on your first product. Build while you're employed. Learn while you're employed. Test while you're employed. Your goal is to start creating evidence that you can generate income from something you own. And if you want somewhere to learn the digital marketing + AI side of building this, that's where AI Creator  Academy comes into the picture for me. But even if you never join— Start with step 1 and 2 today. Your first digital product probably isn’t hiding inside another motivational video.  It’s hiding inside a problem. Someone keeps asking how to solve.  Save this and come back when you’re ready to build yours. Comment “CREATE” if you want the details on the program I used to learn this. #
